_meta.description: Named patient fixtures from PRD Appendix B. Each fixture exercises a specific acceptance scenario. Feed these to the test suite and the demo mode.
_meta.note: All patients are fictional. Any resemblance to real individuals is unintentional.

patients.name: Aarav Kumar
patients.scenario: Paediatric patient — age-banded vital thresholds must differ from adult

expected.note: RR 32 is normal for a 4-year-old (range 18–34). SBP 88 is above the paediatric threshold (70 + 2*4 = 78). An adult-calibrated engine would flag both.

patients.name: Arthur Hale
patients.scenario: Older adult with the same vitals as Aarav — age-specific thresholds should produce different results

expected.note: RR 32 exceeds the adult upper limit of 30. SBP 88 is below the adult threshold of 90. Identical vitals, different patient, different flags.

patients.name: John Doe
patients.scenario: Insufficient vitals to triage — RF11 hard stop

expected.note: Only 1 of 6 triageable vitals recorded. RF11 fires. ATRIA refuses to score — the patient is routed to a clinician, not given a number nobody should trust.
SpO₂ 84% is below the 90% threshold. RF02 fires. Band 1. No model can suppress this.

patients.name: Carlos Rivera
patients.scenario: Respiratory rate exactly at the boundary — confirms SAF-004

expected.note: RR 30 is the upper edge of normal for an adult (rule: >30). RR 31 fires RF13.
HR rising +36, SBP falling −30, SpO₂ falling −4 over 60 minutes. Shock index reaches 1.45. Layer 2 trajectory escalation fires.

patients.name: Thomas Chen
patients.scenario: Long wait — five-hour safeguard within-band modifier

expected.note: Clinically stable ESI 5. After 5 hours (300 minutes) the five-hour safeguard fires as a within-band modifier. It bumps the patient up within their band but does NOT cross a band boundary.

patients.name: Sarah Mitchell
patients.scenario: The recommendation is absent, not hidden, before the nurse commits

expected.note: Before the nurse submits their blind ESI, the API response must not contain atria_esi at all — not null, not hidden, absent.

patients.name: David Park
patients.scenario: Patient deteriorates after initial assessment — worsening report clears sign-off

expected.note: After sign-off, a worsening report forces a fresh blind cycle. The old ATRIA recommendation is discarded — showing it would anchor the next decision.

patients.name: Elena Rodriguez
patients.scenario: Nurse overrides a guardrail flag — reason required, escalation to charge nurse

expected.note: SpO₂ 88% fires RF02. The nurse knows this is the patient's baseline COPD sat. They can override, but must give a reason (known_baseline) and the override is audited.
